differences.title: 1. DEVELOPMENT TEAM
differences.leftDesc: Independent teams own their features and tech stack, boosting agility.
differences.rightDesc: One team manages the entire codebase, potentially causing bottlenecks.

differences.title: 2. CODEBASE ORGANIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Each micro frontend is a separate, manageable unit with its own logic.
differences.rightDesc: All code resides in one large codebase, can become unwieldy.

differences.title: 3. TECHNOLOGY STACK
differences.leftDesc: Different teams can choose best-fit technologies for their micro frontend.
differences.rightDesc: All parts of the frontend use the same technology stack.

differences.title: 4. DEPLOYMENT STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: Micro frontends can be deployed and updated independently of others.
differences.rightDesc: All changes require a single, coordinated deployment of the entire app.

differences.title: 5. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Scale specific parts of the application based on their individual needs.
differences.rightDesc: Scale the entire application, even if only a small part needs it.

differences.title: 6. MAINTENANCE
differences.leftDesc: Maintaining and refactoring smaller, isolated codebases is less risky.
differences.rightDesc: Refactoring a large, intertwined codebase can be extremely challenging.

differences.title: 7. INTEGRATION COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Requires careful planning for communication and integration between micro frontends.
differences.rightDesc: Simpler to get started, but integration complexity grows over time.
